thread:
raj: Heads-up — last 45m we've seen repeated Xid 79 / ECC spikes on several p3a-8x nodes in us-west1. 6 nodes crossed >4 xids/min. I'm prototyping an auto-isolation flow (annotate -> taint -> cordon/drain -> repair) so a noisy one-off doesn't evict important training jobs.

sophie: Can you paste the alert rule and the action plan? need to know the backoff and when we escalate to replacement.

raj: Draft alert rule I'm testing:
```
alert: GPUXidSpike
expr: sum by(node) (increase(nvidia_gpu_xid_total[10m])) > 3
for: 10m
labels: {severity="warning"}
annotations: {runbook="eng-infra/gpu-isolation"}
```

mike: 3 in 10m seems low — kernel/driver transient resets happen. We should avoid draining on single brief spikes (Xid 13s, etc).

alicia: Agreed. Proposal: two-stage flow:
1) soft-isolate: annotate node redwood/gpu-health=degraded + taint redwood/gpu=degraded:NoSchedule so new pods avoid it
2) if signal persists (30m) OR restarts >=2 then cordon + graceful drain + trigger repair pipeline / replacement.

raj: Exactly. For Slurm nodes we mirror state with: 
```
scontrol update NodeName=node-123 State=DRAIN Reason="gpu_xid_spike"
```
and tag the node in the exporter so the alerting rule picks it up.

oncall: How do we avoid killing long-running training without recent checkpoints? We need a pre-drain grace/hook for checkpoint detection.

sophie: Drain sequence for k8s (proposed):
1) kubectl cordon node-xxx
2) kubectl annotate node node-xxx redwood/health=degraded
3) run pre-drain hook: check /var/checkpoints for active, extend
4) kubectl drain node-xxx --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300 --timeout=30m
We add an opt-in label to allow longer grace for known long-training nodes.

raj: infra-bot: automated isolate started for node-3a in us-west1 (reason=gpu.ecc_spike, score=0.81)

raj: paste kernel snippet from node-3a logs: 
```
Mar 17 04:21:13 node-3a kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=0, GPU ID=0
Mar 17 04:21:15 node-3a nvidia-smi: ECC error count increased on GPU0
```

mike: Can we add anomaly scoring instead of raw counts? rolling z-score on error rate + correlate ECC counters, temperature and reboots would reduce false positives.

alicia: Also: retention for raw nvidia-smi + kernel logs for triage. Plan: keep 7 days raw, compressed, then roll up counters. Storage cost is a concern but triage value > cost here.

sophie: Rollout plan: cordon-only in test cluster for 48h, then auto-drain in staging for 2 weeks, then opt-in prod with a 2-region limit and manual approval for replacements.

raj: Add a manual override annotation `redwood/auto-isolate=disabled` for nodes that must be excluded (special hardware, reserved hosts).

oncall: For cost/control: do NOT trigger replacement for preemptible/spot nodes — mark them for maintenance and let autoscaler spin replacements. Also, communicate to capacity team for reserved pools.

mike: Edge case: flapping nodes with low scores. Prefer repeated cordon + repair script (soft repair) over immediate replace. We'll add nightly burn-test job to proactively find flaky cards (small kernel stress + memtest).

sophie: Canary test for the pipeline: inject a synthetic Xid log and ensure alert->annotate->clear path works:
```
# simulate gpu error on test node
logger -p kern.err "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79"
```
Then assert infra-bot annotated and cleared after TTL.

raj: I'll draft the runbook and update infra playbooks with play-by-play and rollback steps.

raj: Action items: @mike implement prometheus rule + infra-bot action wiring; @raj will add Slurm sequence + runbook; @alicia owns log retention/compression policy; @oncall update pager policy.

mike: I'll take prometheus + infra-bot. Will start a PR with the rule and a test alert in staging.

alicia: I'll add compression (zstd) + 7d TTL, and a cheap index for quick queries.

oncall: Pager policy: only page if score>0.9 OR >10 xids in 1h. Otherwise create ticket and slack notify.

infra-bot: action taken: annotated node-3a redwood/health=degraded, tainted redwood/gpu=degraded:NoSchedule

sophie: Thanks — let's sync in infra sync next Tue to review early telemetry and tune thresholds.
